thread:
Mira: Heads up — after the telemetry-proxy roll this morning we're seeing intermittent gaps in DCGM/node_exporter metrics for a subset of GPU nodes (seems bursty, ~30-60s holes). Not every host, but a handful across two racks.

InfraBot: [ALERT] Prometheus firing: dcgm_metric_scrape_failures (firing 6m) — affected targets: 10.0.2.11, 10.0.2.15, 10.0.2.18

Leo: Which proxy version did we roll and to which cluster? Any config changes (rate limits, conn pool)?

Mira: rolled telemetry-proxy v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0 in prod-eu-west-1 earlier at 07:12. The change was the per-host qps limiter and a new upstream connection pooling behaviour. No other k8s changes.

Sam: quick checks: can you paste the proxy logs for an affected pod and also the node_exporter logs from the node? Also run `ss -n sport = :9100` on the node to see connection states.

Mira: pasted small snippets below from the proxy and node exporter: 

```
# telemetry-proxy
{"ts":"2026-03-18T07:14:02Z","level":"warn","msg":"rate limited","path":"/metrics","peer":"10.0.2.15","limit":200,"burst":50}
{"ts":"2026-03-18T07:14:31Z","level":"warn","msg":"upstream conn failed","peer":"10.0.2.11","error":"dial tcp: i/o timeout"}
\n# node_exporter (kubelet sidecar)
level=warn ts=2026-03-18T07:15:05Z msg="scrape_timeout reached for dcgm-exporter" target=10.0.2.15:9100
```

Kevin: v2.4.0 added token-bucket gating that returns 429 + `Retry-After` when it starts throttling. If prom scrapes happen while proxy answers 429, Prom will treat it as a failed scrape. Looks like the NAT/egress window in those racks is amplifying bursts so proxy triggers the limiter.

Oncall: Could be conn tracking or NAT ephemeral exhaustion too. Check `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` and `conntrack -L | wc -l` on one of the affected nodes. Also check for dnat/masquerade limits on the shared egress.

Leo: Can we capture a tcpdump for a short window to prove 429s are coming back from proxy and to see SYN/ACK patterns? Suggested: `kubectl -n infra exec -it telemetry-proxy-pod -- tcpdump -w /tmp/telemetry-proxy.pcap port 443 and host 10.0.2.15` then `kubectl cp` the file.

Mira: did tcpdump and confirmed bursts of `HTTP/1.1 429` interleaved with successful `200` responses. Also noticed Prometheus scrapes overlap (scrape_interval 15s, scrape_timeout 10s) which makes a single 429 drop a hard failure.

Sam: short-term mitigation options: 1) revert telemetry-proxy to v2.3.1 to remove gating, 2) increase scrape_timeout to 15s for dcgm targets, 3) add a small jitter to scrape_interval to avoid synchronous bursts. Long-term: tune token-bucket parameters and upstream connection pool sizing.

Kevin: I'm +1 on tuning token bucket first (increase burst and refill) and also adding a proxy-side circuit-breaker so sustained failures return 503 quickly instead of throttling everything.

Mira: I'll open a small rollback PR now for the proxy (can revert if anyone objects). Also creating a Prometheus scrape-jitter job to test changing scrape_interval to 15±3s for the DCGM job.

Oncall: If rollback isn't fast enough, runbook step: 1) scale telemetry-proxy to 0 and back up for canary (kubectl -n infra scale deploy telemetry-proxy --replicas=0 && sleep 10 && kubectl -n infra scale deploy telemetry-proxy --replicas=3), 2) patch scrape config with larger timeout and jitter, 3) monitor alert for 10m.

Mira: filing incident for tracking + I'll paste the rollback PR link in a sec. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

InfraBot: Incident created — INC-20260318-77 (stream: eng-infra) — assigned to Mira, priority P2.

Leo: After this stabilizes let's add an observability dashboard tile: "proxy 429 rate / target" and a per-rack conntrack high-watermark alert so we catch NAT exhaustion earlier.

Sam: Good call. Also document the proxy token-bucket defaults in infra runbook so next rollout doesn't surprise on default limits.

Mira: Agree — will add runbook notes and a follow-up ticket for dashboard + runbook.
